newsitem.title: USA: Harvard Industries sees 1997 net loss.
newsitem.headline: Harvard Industries sees 1997 net loss.

text.p: Harvard Industries Inc said on Wednesday it expected to report a net loss for the second quarter and the year ended September 30, 1997, with flat or slightly higher second quarter sales.
The company reported a current first quarter earnings loss of $4.90 per share compared to a loss of $0.78 per share in the same quarter last year.

It cited continued operational inefficiencies at its Doehler-Jarvis subsidiary, the effects of the October 1996 General Motors Corp strike, softness in some large passenger car sales, a sales decline at Harman Automotive and continued high interest expense and goodwill amortization.
Harvard said it was involved in a due diligence process with a potential buyer for the assets of Harman Automotive and it was continuing to try and sell its furniture segment.

The company also said it was continuing to investigate other strategic alternatives, including the sale of certain assets and businesses. It said it had retained investment bankers The Blackstone Group.

Harvard said Ford, effective January 1997, would resource about $8 million in sales during the year ended September 30, 1996 to a competitor due to the inability of the Doehler-Jarvis Toledo Plant to maintain delivery dates compatible with customer demands.
Harvard said it believed this action resulted from the overcapacity at the Doehler plant and it was taking steps to eliminate operating inefficiencies there.
After completing this program, it said production efficiencies would improve and the company would achieve a reduction in certain costs.

Harvard also said based on current projections, it expected to use its line of credit to the maximum available under the CIT Group/business financing agreement for the balance of the year ending September 30, 1997.
It also expected its accounts receivable collateral would exceed collateral required under the borrowing limits of its financing agreement.
Harvard said it had preliminary discussions with the CIT Group/Business Credit over increasing the company's line of credit, to permit using the additional projected borrowing capacity if necessary.
